task: Explore: build a cooperative-game cost-sharing tool (Shapley value, nucleolus, core) as a research-algorithm venture

errors.what: First nucleolus solved the primal stage LP (2^n rows) with Bland's rule: 62 s for 10 members; Dantzig pricing still 7-20 s.
errors.fix: Solve each stage's dual (n+1 rows); 10-45 ms, identical to the reference.

errors.what: Two test expectations were wrong (a group priced at 30 vs a split at 24 is correctly flagged; 'A,x' alone reads as a header).
errors.fix: Corrected the tests, not the engine.

errors.what: Local CI (run_workflow_locally --for-changes) caught three things in the new venture: Math.max(...array) spreads (check_row_spread), no inbound sibling link (siblings.mjs, budget 0), and a CSV export without a formula-injection guard (check_csv_formula_guard).
errors.fix: reduce() instead of spreads; ranked-ballot-counter's footer links the tool (both group-decision tools) with a page.test assertion; csvCell guard plus a test. Re-run: all triggered workflows pass.

doc_friction.issue: 'ships a real public dataset as its example' has no guidance for methods whose natural inputs (coalition prices, road distances) have no public dataset; used the Mishnah's claims as the real example and labelled the other two as made up.

The definition-of-done table does not mention three gates every new tool hits (inbound sibling link, CSV formula guard, no array spreads into Math.min/max); each cost a CI round trip. Listing them, or a scaffold that ships them, would save the next new-tool run.
The first --for-changes run was voided because I edited a page while it ran (it says so clearly); running it with --foreground after the last edit avoids that.

deviations.why: Two of the three examples (shared road, three towns) are made-up numbers; no public dataset of coalition costs was available without paywalled papers.
deviations.did: Real public-domain example for the claims mode (Mishnah Ketubot 10:4, with its published answer as a test); the others are labelled 'made-up numbers' on the page, in example-data.mjs and data/SOURCE.md.
deviations.result: The real example doubles as the strongest test (Talmud rule and LP nucleolus agree with the Mishnah).

notes: Explore idea: cooperative game theory as a research-algorithm tool (ventures/cost-sharing-calculator); no venture README mentioned Shapley/nucleolus/core (1,387 searched). Shapley (exact, 14 members), nucleolus by Maschler-Peleg-Shapley sequential LPs solved through their duals with a hand-written two-phase simplex (10 members, 10-45 ms), SCRB/ENSC, core check naming the most-overcharged subgroup; road mode (Littlechild & Owen closed form, any size, prefix core check); claims mode (Talmud rule = nucleolus, random arrival = Shapley). Verified vs independent scipy HiGHS reference on 40 games (<=5e-12), Mishnah's three estates, glove game, textbook LP. DOIs checked against Crossref. Chromium at 1200/390 px: no console errors, no external requests. Local checks: run_venture_tests cost-sharing-calculator 39/39 and ranked-ballot-counter 37/37 pass; run_workflow_locally --for-changes after fixes: every triggered workflow passes (control-plane, prompts-ci, checklist, conflict-markers, doc-refs, duplicate-symbols, link-contrast, readme-live-links, sibling-links 2/2, page-integrity, agent-permission-harness, pages 6/6, ventures-tests 5/5, portfolio-validate 99/99, portfolio-pages 12/12; uses: steps not run locally).

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

human_equivalent.basis: estimate: a developer implementing Shapley, a nucleolus LP pipeline with its own simplex, three modes, a page, CLI, independent Python reference and tests

certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured
